ai.literal: Prospering fate-by appears sluggishness-absence; hand-wealth going fate-by appears laziness.
ai.translation: Through the fate that brings prosperity, tireless effort arises. Through the fate that takes away accumulated wealth, laziness arises.
ai.modern: செல்வம் பெருகுவதற்கான ஊழ் இருக்கும்போது தளராத முயற்சி உண்டாகும். கையில் உள்ள செல்வம் அழிவதற்கான ஊழ் இருக்கும்போது சோம்பல் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how destiny operates by influencing a person's mindset and actions. The phrase 'ஆகு ஊழ்' refers to a fate of prospering, which naturally brings about 'அசைவின்மை' (the absence of sluggishness, or tireless effort). Conversely, when the fate of losing ('போகு ஊழ்') one's accumulated wealth ('கைப்பொருள்') is active, 'மடி' (laziness) takes over. Thus, destiny shapes outcomes by instilling either industriousness or sloth.

ai.literal: Ignorance will-cause loss fate; knowledge will-expand prospering fate reached time.
ai.translation: The fate that brings loss will cause a person to become ignorant. The fate that brings prosperity, when it arrives, will expand their knowledge.
ai.modern: அழிவைத் தரும் ஊழ்வினை வரும்போது அது ஒருவனை அறிவற்றவனாக்குகிறது; ஆக்கத்தைத் தரும் ஊழ்வினை வரும்போது அது அவனது அறிவை விரிவடையச் செய்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how destiny directly influences human intellect and decision-making. The fate of loss clouds a person's judgment, causing them to act foolishly and bring about their own ruin. Conversely, when the fate of prosperity arrives, it expands their wisdom, guiding them naturally toward success. The word 'அகற்றும்' typically means 'removes' or 'dispels', but in this specific context, it takes the sense of 'widens' or 'expands' to contrast with the ignorance caused by bad fate.

ai.literal: Subtle texts many even if learned, nevertheless one's own innate knowledge indeed will prevail.
ai.translation: Even if one learns many profound texts, one's innate knowledge will ultimately prevail.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் பல நுட்பமான நூல்களைக் கற்றாலும், இறுதியில் அவனது இயற்கையான அறிவே மேலோங்கி நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that formal education cannot completely override one's natural disposition or destiny. The word 'uṇmai' usually means 'truth', but in the context of this chapter on fate, it takes the sense of 'innate' or 'natural'. Therefore, 'uṇmai aṟivu' refers to the inherent understanding a person possesses, which will ultimately dominate their actions despite studying many profound texts.

ai.literal: Two different [are] the world's nature: wealth [is] different, clear-minded ones becoming also [is] different.
ai.translation: The nature of the world takes two different forms: the amassing of wealth is one thing, and the attainment of clear wisdom is another.
ai.modern: உலகத்தின் இயற்கை இரண்டு வேறுபட்ட நிலைகளைக் கொண்டது: செல்வம் உடையவராக இருப்பது வேறு, தெளிந்த அறிவுடையவராக இருப்பது வேறு.
ai.explanation: This couplet observes the fundamental disconnect between material wealth and intellectual clarity in the world. The phrase 'இருவேறு இயற்கை' (two different natures) establishes that the world operates on divergent paths. 'திரு' (wealth) and 'தெள்ளியர் ஆதல்' (becoming clear-minded) are explicitly contrasted as 'வேறு... வேறு' (different... different). It implies that the forces of destiny distribute riches and wisdom independently, so that the wealthy are not necessarily wise, and the wise are not necessarily wealthy.

ai.literal: Good things all bad become, bad things even good become, wealth for making.
ai.translation: In the pursuit of wealth, all good things may turn bad, and even bad things may turn good.
ai.modern: செல்வத்தை ஈட்ட முயலும்போது, விதியின் காரணமாக நல்ல சூழ்நிலைகள் எல்லாம் தீயவையாக மாறிவிடும்; தீய சூழ்நிலைகளும் நல்லவையாக மாறி வெற்றியைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the unpredictable power of fate in human endeavors, particularly in acquiring wealth. It states that when destiny is unfavorable, even the most favorable circumstances and good strategies will turn into failures. Conversely, when destiny is favorable, even adverse conditions and poor plans will transform into successes. The contrasting pairs of good and bad highlight how human calculation is ultimately subordinate to the natural order of fate.

ai.literal: Even if guarded, they will not become (one's own), things that are not (one's) portion; having driven out and even if poured away, they will not go, one's own things.
ai.translation: Things not destined for you will not stay, no matter how carefully you guard them. Your own destined things will not leave, even if you cast them away.
ai.modern: நமக்கு விதியாக விதிக்கப்படாத பொருள்கள், நாம் எவ்வளவுதான் பாதுகாத்தாலும் நம்மிடம் தங்காது. நமக்கு உரிய பொருள்கள், நாமே வெளியே கொண்டுபோய் வீசினாலும் நம்மை விட்டுப் போகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the inescapable nature of destiny regarding wealth and possessions. The word 'பால்' refers to the portion or lot assigned to a person by fate. If something is not meant to be yours, no amount of guarding ('பரியினும்') will make it stay. Conversely, what is truly yours ('தம') cannot be lost, even if you deliberately throw it away ('உய்த்துச் சொரியினும்').

ai.literal: He who apportioned - apportioned - way - except - ten million - to those who amassed - enjoying - is rare.
ai.translation: Even for those who have amassed ten million, it is impossible to enjoy it except in the manner ordained by the Apportioner.
ai.modern: விதியை வகுத்தவன் வகுத்தபடி அல்லாமல், கோடிப் பொருளைச் சேர்த்தவர்க்கும் அதனை அனுபவிப்பது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: The couplet states that human enjoyment of wealth is strictly bound by destiny. The word 'vakuttāṉ' refers to the one who apportions or ordains, representing the personification of fate. Even if a person successfully gathers 'kōṭi' (ten million) units of wealth, they cannot simply consume or enjoy it at will. The act of 'tuyttal' (enjoying) is only possible in the exact 'vakai' (manner or measure) that has been pre-ordained.

ai.literal: Will renounce indeed, enjoyment those without, things destined to be experienced without feeding will pass if.
ai.translation: Even those without worldly enjoyments would renounce the world, if the experiences destined for them would pass away without forcing themselves upon them.
ai.modern: தாம் அனுபவிக்க வேண்டிய வினைகள் தங்களை அனுபவிக்கச் செய்யாமல் தாமாகவே கழிந்துபோகுமானால், வறுமையில் உள்ளவர்கள் கூட உலக வாழ்க்கையைத் துறந்து விடுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the inescapable power of destiny. It observes that people who lack wealth and worldly enjoyments ('துப்புரவு இல்லார்') have little reason to remain attached to worldly life, yet they do not easily become ascetics. The reason is that destiny does not simply pass away ('கழியும்'); it actively forces individuals to undergo their allotted experiences ('உறற்பால'). The word 'ஊட்டா' (without feeding) vividly personifies destiny as an entity that insists on feeding people their destined joys and sorrows, thereby keeping even the destitute bound to the world.

ai.literal: Good when becoming as good things those who see, bad when becoming sorrow experiencing why?
ai.translation: Those who gladly accept good fortune as a natural occurrence, why should they suffer sorrow when bad fortune strikes?
ai.modern: நன்மைகள் நடக்கும்போது அவற்றை இயல்பான நல்லவையாக ஏற்றுக்கொள்பவர்கள், தீமைகள் நடக்கும்போது மட்டும் துன்பப்பட்டு கலங்குவது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the inconsistency in human behavior regarding fate. When destiny brings good things, people readily accept them as natural and positive. Therefore, the poet asks why the same people feel sorrowful and distressed when destiny inevitably brings misfortune. The word அன்று usually means 'not that', but here it is used as the direct opposite of நன்று (good) to mean bad or evil fortune. Recognizing that both good and bad are part of the same natural order helps one maintain equanimity.

ai.literal: Than fate, great strength what are there? Other one even if devised, it will precede.
ai.translation: What is more powerful than fate? Even if you devise another way, fate itself steps in first.
ai.modern: ஊழை விட மிகுந்த வலிமையுடையவை வேறு எவை உள்ளன? ஊழை விலக்க வேறு ஒரு வழியை நாம் திட்டமிட்டாலும், அந்த ஊழே முன்னே வந்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet asks a rhetorical question about the supreme power of fate or the natural order of things. It states that there is absolutely nothing stronger than fate. The word 'சூழினும்' means 'even if one plans or devises' a countermeasure to avoid what is destined. In such cases, 'தான்' (fate itself) will 'முந்துறும்' (arrive first or take precedence), ensuring that human plans are overridden by the destined outcome.
